If the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (the stronger version of the Riemann Hypothesis) is proven, these become proven facts:
Algorithms that no longer need randomness
- Primality testing: Miller's fast test becomes proven correct with no randomness
- Square roots mod a prime: becomes solvable fast and with no coin flips (today that's an open problem)
- Cube roots and other roots mod a prime: same.
- Factoring polynomials over finite fields: almost fast (quasi-polynomial) with no randomness, instead of needing randomness
- Building finite fields: you can construct any finite field directly, with no random search
- Factoring vs. (n): factoring a number becomes provably as easy as computing on), even without randomness
- Primes with a given remainder: a prime with any allowed remainder mod q exists that's at most about q, so searching for one is fast
Complexity theory
- Polynomial equations:idoes this system of equations have a solution?" drops from
PSPACE to a much lower class (AM)
- Algebraic P vs NP: Valiant's algebraic version of P vs NP gets tied to the normal P vs NP over the complex numbers
- Turing machines: a known 744-state Turing machine is proven to run forever

Complexity theory
- Polynomial equations: does this system of equations have a solution?" drops from PSPACE to a much lower class (AM)
- Algebraic P vs NP: Valiant's algebraic version of P vs NP gets tied to the normal P vs NP over the complex numbers
- Turing machines: a known 744-state Turing machine is proven to run torever
Number theory software
- Math libraries: PARI/GP and Magma results computed "assuming GRH" become fully proven
- Class groups: algorithms that compute these number-field structures get guaranteed running times
- Elliptic curve generation: the algorithms used to create curves for crypto get guaranteed running times
Cryptography (no new attacks, only proofs)
- Elliptic curves: proven that if discrete log is hard on one curve, it's hard on almost all similar curves
- Lattice crypto: known quantum attacks on some lattice schemes become proven to work

- Isogeny crypto: known quantum attacks on some isogeny schemes get proven speeds
- Code-based crypto: schemes like BIKE get the guarantee that the special primes they need exist
Prime gaps
- Next prime: there's always one within about Vp log p of p, so "find the next prime" has a guaranteed worst case
What it does NOT do
- It doesn't solve P vs NP
- It doesn't make factoring easy, so RSA and elliptic-curve crypto stay safe
- It doesn't make anything faster in practice, because randomized versions already work
today
- Ramanujan graphs, expanders and AG codes are unaffected: they use a finite-field version of RH that was proven decades ago

Mud. In the days before computers we had mud. You couldn't send messages on mud but you could play games on it. On Saturday mornings we went looking for mud – great piles of fresh mud straight from the builder's truck; mud we made ourselves from soil and water; mud scooped from the beds of ponds and streams. We ran through mud and jumped in mud. We clambered up mud and slid down mud. We rolled in mud and sat on mud. Grown-ups didn't like mud. They wouldn't allow it in the house. They wore protective clothing, They scrubbed it off trousers and washed it off cars. But I liked mud. You couldn't save data on mud but there were many different levels and it was always dirt cheap.
